title: Egg roll with chicken or turkey

content.title: About
content.content: Egg roll is a crispy roll made from thin dough, filled with tender chicken or turkey meat, vegetables, and aromatic spices. The dough is fried to a golden crust while the filling stays juicy and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg roll originates from Asian street food culture and is commonly served in food stalls.
The turkey version was created as a leaner alternative to the traditional chicken filling.
The dough is a simple mixture of flour, water and salt, without eggs.
Traditionally the rolls are served with soy sauce, sweet chili or vinegar.
Some regional recipes add finely diced pineapple for a subtle sweetness.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey provide complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in fat (turkey)
items.content: Turkey contains less saturated fat than chicken, making it a better choice for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is rich in B3 and B6 vitamins, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Vegetable content
items.content: Added vegetables (cabbage, carrot, onion) provide fiber, vitamins and antioxidants.

items.title: Allergy to chicken/turkey
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to poultry, experiencing skin reactions or digestive issues.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce used in preparation can raise the salt level; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Trans fats in fried dough
items.content: Deep‑frying can create trans fats; choosing rolls fried in low‑temperature vegetable oil reduces this risk.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The crispy dough makes the roll energy‑dense; moderation is advised for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Egg roll is convenient to eat by hand as a snack or light meal. Serve it with soy sauce, sweet chili, vinegar, or a yogurt‑based dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared rolls in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness before serving.
